question: A research agent runs for several hours, repeatedly retrieving and discussing documents, and the conversation is approaching its context window limit while still needing to reference earlier findings. Which strategy matches this query pattern?
options: A) Switch to a model with a smaller context window to force more frequent manual summarization by the user.
B) Enable server-side compaction so earlier turns are automatically summarized while the session continues past the limit.
C) Re-upload every previously retrieved document at the start of each new turn so nothing is lost from history.
D) Increase max_tokens on each request so more output room is reserved for new retrieval results.
correct_answers: B) Enable server-side compaction so earlier turns are automatically summarized while the session continues past the limit.
explanations: Deliberately choosing a smaller context window shrinks the working space available and shifts summarization work onto the user instead of using built-in context management.

Correct. Server-side compaction is the primary mechanism for long-running, retrieval-heavy sessions approaching the context limit: it summarizes earlier turns automatically so the conversation can continue while preserving prior findings.
Re-uploading every prior document each turn accelerates hitting the context limit rather than managing it, and duplicates content already in the conversation history.
Raising max_tokens changes how much a single turn can output, not how much accumulated conversation history fits in the window, so it does not address the approaching limit.
